description: Manage an email subscriber list from hygiene standards through segmentation and health tracking.

steps.description: Define the hygiene standards for the email list including bounce handling, unsubscribe processing, and inactive removal rules.

inputs.name: current-list-size
inputs.desc: Current number of subscribers on the list

inputs.name: list-platform
inputs.desc: The email service provider or platform hosting the list

outputs.name: hygiene-policy
outputs.desc: Documented rules for bounce handling, unsubscribe processing, and inactive removal

outputs.name: cleaning-schedule
outputs.desc: Frequency and scope of list cleaning runs

process: Set the hard bounce removal rule (remove after first hard bounce).
Set the soft bounce threshold (remove after N consecutive soft bounces within a time window).
Define the unsubscribe processing standard (immediate removal, confirmation page, feedback survey).
Define the inactive subscriber threshold (no opens or clicks in N days) and the removal or re-engagement trigger.

steps.description: Segment the subscriber list by engagement level and demographic or behavioral attributes.

outputs.name: segment-definitions
outputs.desc: Named segments with inclusion criteria

outputs.name: segment-sizes
outputs.desc: Current count per segment

process: Create engagement-based segments: highly engaged (opened or clicked in last 30 days), engaged (last 90 days), at-risk (90 to 180 days), dormant (over 180 days).
Create attribute-based segments using available data (source, signup date, location, purchase history, interests).
Cross-reference engagement and attribute segments to identify high-value sub-groups.
Document the segment definitions and current counts.

steps.description: Run a list cleaning pass based on the hygiene policy.

inputs.name: segment-definitions
inputs.desc: Segment criteria for identifying inactive subscribers

outputs.name: cleaning-results
outputs.desc: Count of records removed by reason (hard bounce, soft bounce, unsubscribe, inactive)

outputs.name: cleaned-list-size
outputs.desc: Subscriber count after cleaning

process: Remove all hard bounced addresses.
Remove addresses exceeding the soft bounce threshold.
Process pending unsubscribe requests.
Flag or remove dormant subscribers per the inactive threshold.
Log all removals with reason codes.

steps.description: Manage subscriber preferences and consent records.

outputs.name: preference-center-spec
outputs.desc: Design for the subscriber preference center (frequency, topics, format)

outputs.name: consent-audit
outputs.desc: Audit of consent status across the list (opted-in, single opt-in, double opt-in, unknown)

process: Inventory the preference options to offer (email frequency, content topics, email format).
Audit the current consent status of all subscribers.
Design the preference center page.
Document the consent record retention policy.

steps.description: Track and report on list health metrics over time.

inputs.name: cleaning-results
inputs.desc: Results from the latest cleaning pass

inputs.name: consent-audit
inputs.desc: Current consent status across the list

outputs.name: list-health-report
outputs.desc: Report covering growth rate, churn rate, engagement distribution, deliverability indicators, and consent compliance

outputs.name: list-management-plan
outputs.desc: The complete list management plan with standards, segments, cleaning schedule, and metrics

process: Calculate the list growth rate (new subscribers minus removals over the period).
Calculate the churn rate (unsubscribes plus bounces divided by total).
Report the engagement distribution across segments.
Report the deliverability indicators (bounce rate, complaint rate).
Compile the full list management plan.

description: Optimize email deliverability from infrastructure audit through content checks and inbox placement monitoring.

steps.description: Audit the email sending infrastructure including authentication records and IP reputation.

inputs.name: sending-domain
inputs.desc: The domain used for sending email

inputs.name: sending-platform
inputs.desc: The email service provider or SMTP infrastructure

outputs.name: infrastructure-audit
outputs.desc: Status of SPF, DKIM, DMARC, IP reputation, and sending domain health

outputs.name: infrastructure-fixes
outputs.desc: List of issues found and recommended fixes

process: Check SPF record for correctness and alignment.
Check DKIM signing and key rotation status.
Check DMARC policy and reporting configuration.
Assess IP reputation using blacklist checks and sender score.
Document all findings and fixes needed.

steps.description: Check email content for spam triggers that could hurt deliverability.

outputs.name: content-audit
outputs.desc: List of spam trigger issues found in recent sends (words, formatting, image ratio, link density)

outputs.name: content-guidelines
outputs.desc: Guidelines for avoiding spam triggers in future sends

process: Review recent email content for spam trigger words and phrases.
Check the text-to-image ratio (aim for at least 60% text).
Check link density and URL reputation.
Review the from name, subject line patterns, and preheader text.
Compile the content guidelines document.

steps.description: Plan and execute an IP or domain warmup for new sending infrastructure.

inputs.name: infrastructure-fixes
inputs.desc: Fixes applied to the sending infrastructure

inputs.name: content-guidelines
inputs.desc: Content guidelines to follow during warmup

outputs.name: warmup-plan
outputs.desc: Day-by-day warmup schedule with volume targets and ISP distribution

outputs.name: warmup-metrics
outputs.desc: Tracking metrics during warmup (delivery rate, bounce rate, complaint rate per day)

process: Determine the target daily sending volume after warmup.
Build the warmup schedule starting at a low volume and doubling every 2 to 3 days.
Select the most engaged subscribers for early warmup sends.
Define the abort criteria (bounce rate above 5%, complaint rate above 0.1%).
Document the warmup plan.

steps.description: Monitor inbox placement rates across major mailbox providers.

outputs.name: placement-report
outputs.desc: Inbox vs spam vs missing placement rates by mailbox provider

outputs.name: deliverability-report
outputs.desc: Full deliverability optimization report with infrastructure, content, warmup, and placement findings

process: Measure inbox placement rates by provider (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, Apple Mail).
Identify providers where placement is below target.
Diagnose the cause (reputation, content, authentication, engagement).
Recommend corrective actions per provider.
Compile the full deliverability report.

description: Publish a recurring newsletter from editorial planning through performance analysis.

steps.description: Plan the editorial calendar for the newsletter including topics, cadence, and content sources.

inputs.name: newsletter-goals
inputs.desc: The purpose and audience for the newsletter

inputs.name: publishing-cadence
inputs.desc: How often the newsletter will be sent (weekly, biweekly, monthly)

outputs.name: editorial-calendar
outputs.desc: Calendar of upcoming newsletter issues with topics and deadlines

outputs.name: content-sources
outputs.desc: List of content sources to draw from for each issue

process: Define the newsletter sections and recurring features.
Plan topics for the next 4 to 8 issues based on audience interests and business goals.
Identify content sources for each section (internal updates, curated links, original writing, user contributions).
Set the production timeline (content deadline, design deadline, review deadline, send date).

steps.description: Gather and curate the content for a single newsletter issue.

inputs.name: editorial-calendar
inputs.desc: The editorial plan for this issue

outputs.name: curated-content
outputs.desc: Selected and organized content for the issue

outputs.name: content-brief
outputs.desc: Brief for any original content that needs to be written

process: Collect content from each identified source.
Select the best items based on relevance, timeliness, and audience interest.
Write the brief for any original sections that need drafting.
Organize the content in the planned section order.

steps.description: Write the newsletter copy and assemble the design.

outputs.name: newsletter-draft
outputs.desc: The complete newsletter draft ready for review

outputs.name: design-assets
outputs.desc: Images, headers, and layout elements used

process: Write the original content sections from the briefs.
Write the intros, transitions, and CTAs for curated sections.
Assemble the content into the email template.
Add images, headers, and design elements.

steps.description: Test the newsletter rendering across email clients and devices.

outputs.name: render-test-results
outputs.desc: Screenshots and issues found across email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, mobile)

outputs.name: approved-newsletter
outputs.desc: The final approved newsletter ready to send

process: Send test emails to preview accounts across major clients.
Check rendering on desktop and mobile for each client.
Verify all links work and tracking is in place.
Fix any rendering issues and get final approval.

steps.description: Schedule the send, then analyze the performance after delivery.

outputs.name: send-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation of send with timestamp and recipient count

outputs.name: newsletter-performance-report
outputs.desc: Performance report covering open rate, click rate, unsubscribe rate, and top-clicked links

process: Schedule the send for the optimal time based on audience data.
Monitor the initial delivery metrics (bounces, complaints).
After 48 hours, pull the open rate, click rate, click-to-open rate, and unsubscribe rate.
Identify the top-clicked links and most engaging sections.
Compile the performance report.

description: Manage the email subscriber lifecycle from welcome through re-engagement and sunset.

steps.description: Design the welcome email sequence for new subscribers.

inputs.name: subscriber-source
inputs.desc: Where new subscribers come from (signup form, lead magnet, purchase, event)

inputs.name: brand-voice
inputs.desc: The brand voice and tone guidelines

outputs.name: welcome-sequence
outputs.desc: The welcome email sequence (timing, subject, content outline for each email)

outputs.name: welcome-goals
outputs.desc: The goals for the welcome sequence (activation, engagement, conversion)

process: Define the number of emails in the welcome sequence (typically 3 to 5).
Write the content outline for each email (introduction, value delivery, engagement prompt, conversion offer).
Set the timing between emails (typically 1, 3, 5, 7 days after signup).
Define the success metrics for the welcome sequence.

steps.description: Segment subscribers by engagement level and track movement between segments.

outputs.name: engagement-segments
outputs.desc: Defined engagement segments with thresholds (active, at-risk, dormant)

outputs.name: segment-movement-report
outputs.desc: Report showing how subscribers move between engagement levels over time

process: Define the engagement scoring criteria (opens, clicks, replies, purchases weighted by recency).
Set the thresholds for each segment (active, at-risk, dormant).
Calculate the current distribution across segments.
Track the movement between segments month over month.

steps.description: Design and trigger re-engagement campaigns for dormant subscribers.

inputs.name: segment-movement-report
inputs.desc: Data on subscribers entering the dormant segment

outputs.name: re-engagement-campaigns
outputs.desc: The re-engagement email sequences with triggers, content, and incentives

outputs.name: re-engagement-results
outputs.desc: Results of re-engagement campaigns (reactivated, still dormant, unsubscribed)

process: Design the re-engagement trigger (subscriber enters the dormant segment).
Write the re-engagement email sequence (we miss you, last chance, preference update, final notice).
Set the incentive strategy (exclusive content, discount, survey).
Measure the reactivation rate and cost per reactivation.

steps.description: Manage the sunset policy for permanently removing inactive subscribers.

inputs.name: re-engagement-results
inputs.desc: Results showing subscribers who did not re-engage

outputs.name: sunset-policy
outputs.desc: The documented sunset policy with timeline and criteria

outputs.name: lifecycle-management-plan
outputs.desc: Complete subscriber lifecycle management plan covering welcome, engagement, re-engagement, and sunset

process: Define the sunset timeline (remove subscribers who do not respond to the re-engagement sequence).
Set the grace period before final removal.
Document the removal process and record retention.
Compile the full lifecycle management plan.

description: Build a reusable email template system from brand guidelines through a tested template library.

steps.description: Define the brand guidelines specific to email design.

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: The existing brand guidelines (colors, fonts, logo)

inputs.name: email-use-cases
inputs.desc: The types of emails to be sent (newsletter, promotional, transactional, event)

outputs.name: email-brand-spec
outputs.desc: Email-specific brand guidelines covering colors, fonts, layout rules, and logo placement

outputs.name: template-requirements
outputs.desc: Requirements for each email type (sections, CTAs, footer, legal requirements)

process: Adapt the brand colors for email (web-safe colors, dark mode considerations).
Select the email-safe fonts (system fonts and web fonts with fallbacks).
Define the layout grid and spacing rules for email.
Define the logo placement, CTA button styles, and footer requirements.
Document the legal requirements per email type (unsubscribe link, physical address, privacy link).

steps.description: Create the master email templates for each use case.

outputs.name: template-set
outputs.desc: The master templates for newsletter, transactional, promotional, and event emails

outputs.name: template-documentation
outputs.desc: Usage guide for each template including editable sections and content rules

process: Build the newsletter template with header, content sections, sidebar, and footer.
Build the transactional template with minimal design and clear action focus.
Build the promotional template with hero image, offer section, and CTA.
Build the event template with date, location, agenda, and registration CTA.
Document the editable sections and content rules for each.

steps.description: Test all templates across email clients and devices.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Rendering results across clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, Yahoo) on desktop and mobile

outputs.name: template-fixes
outputs.desc: Issues found and fixes applied

process: Test each template in Gmail (web and mobile), Outlook (desktop and web), Apple Mail, and Yahoo.
Check dark mode rendering in each client.
Verify responsive behavior on mobile screens.
Fix any rendering issues and retest.

steps.description: Publish the templates to the template library with usage documentation.

outputs.name: template-library
outputs.desc: The published template library accessible to the team

outputs.name: template-system-document
outputs.desc: Complete template system document with brand spec, templates, testing results, and usage guide

process: Upload each template to the email platform's template library.
Set permissions and access controls.
Publish the usage documentation alongside each template.
Compile the full template system document.

description: Set up transactional emails from inventory through trigger configuration and delivery monitoring.

steps.description: Inventory all transactional email types needed by the application or business.

inputs.name: application-context
inputs.desc: The product or service that sends transactional emails

inputs.name: user-journey-map
inputs.desc: The key user actions that trigger emails

outputs.name: email-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all transactional email types with trigger events, recipient, and priority

outputs.name: content-requirements
outputs.desc: Content requirements for each email (data fields, personalization, legal copy)

process: Map the user journey to identify every trigger point (signup, purchase, password reset, shipping, renewal, cancellation).
Classify each email by category (account, order, notification, security).
Define the priority and delivery SLA for each (security emails within seconds, order confirmations within minutes).
Document the dynamic data fields needed in each email.

steps.description: Write the content for each transactional email.

inputs.name: email-inventory
inputs.desc: The list of transactional emails to write

outputs.name: email-content
outputs.desc: Written content for each transactional email (subject, preheader, body, CTA)

outputs.name: personalization-map
outputs.desc: Map of dynamic fields and merge tags for each email

process: Write the subject line and preheader for each email.
Write the body copy with clear action focus and minimal design.
Insert the merge tags for personalization.
Write the fallback content for missing data fields.

steps.description: Configure the sending service and event triggers for each transactional email.

outputs.name: trigger-configuration
outputs.desc: Configured triggers linking application events to email sends

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results of trigger testing for each email type

process: Configure the API or webhook integration between the application and the email service.
Map each application event to its corresponding email template.
Set the sending parameters (from address, reply-to, priority, rate limits).
Test each trigger by simulating the application event and verifying delivery.

steps.description: Set up delivery monitoring and alerting for transactional emails.

outputs.name: monitoring-setup
outputs.desc: Monitoring dashboards and alerts for transactional email delivery

outputs.name: transactional-email-setup-document
outputs.desc: Complete setup document covering inventory, content, triggers, and monitoring

process: Set up delivery rate monitoring by email type.
Configure alerts for delivery failures, high bounce rates, or latency spikes.
Establish the escalation process for delivery incidents.
Compile the full transactional email setup document.

description: Run an email A/B testing program from roadmap through execution and documentation of learnings.

steps.description: Define the testing roadmap covering what to test and in what order.

inputs.name: email-performance-data
inputs.desc: Current email performance metrics (open rates, click rates, conversion rates)

inputs.name: testing-goals
inputs.desc: What the testing program aims to improve

outputs.name: testing-roadmap
outputs.desc: Ordered list of tests to run (subject lines, send times, content, CTAs, design)

outputs.name: testing-priorities
outputs.desc: Tests ranked by expected impact and ease of execution

process: Identify the biggest performance gaps (low open rate means test subjects, low click rate means test content and CTAs).
List all testable elements: subject lines, preheaders, send times, send days, from names, content length, CTA placement, CTA copy, design layout, personalization.
Rank by expected impact and ease of execution.
Schedule the tests across upcoming sends.

steps.description: Calculate the sample size and set significance thresholds for each test.

outputs.name: test-parameters
outputs.desc: Sample size, split ratio, significance level, and minimum detectable effect for each test

outputs.name: test-schedule
outputs.desc: When each test runs and how long to wait before declaring a winner

process: Calculate the minimum sample size for the desired significance level (typically 95%) and minimum detectable effect.
Set the split ratio (50/50 for two variants, or holdout percentage for multi-variant).
Determine the observation period based on sending volume and sample size.
Document the decision criteria for declaring a winner.

steps.description: Execute the A/B test and collect the results.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Raw results for each variant (opens, clicks, conversions, unsubscribes)

outputs.name: statistical-analysis
outputs.desc: Statistical significance calculation and confidence interval

process: Configure the test in the email platform with the defined variants and split.
Send to the test audience.
Wait for the observation period to complete.
Pull the results for each variant.

steps.description: Analyze results, apply the winner, and document the learnings.

outputs.name: test-winner
outputs.desc: The winning variant with performance delta and confidence level

outputs.name: testing-program-report
outputs.desc: Cumulative report of all tests, results, and learnings to date

process: Determine the winner based on the primary metric and statistical significance.
Apply the winning variant to future sends.
Document the learning (what was tested, what won, by how much, and the hypothesis for why).
Update the testing roadmap with the next test based on these learnings.

description: Plan internal email communications from audience segmentation through template creation and engagement tracking.

steps.description: Identify the internal audience segments and their communication needs.

inputs.name: organization-structure
inputs.desc: The organizational structure (departments, teams, levels, locations)

inputs.name: communication-goals
inputs.desc: What the internal communications program aims to achieve

outputs.name: audience-segments
outputs.desc: Defined internal audience segments with size and communication needs

outputs.name: communication-types
outputs.desc: Types of internal communications needed (all-hands update, department news, leadership message, policy update, event notice)

process: Map the organization into audience segments (all employees, department, leadership, location, project team).
Identify the communication types each segment needs.
Set the priority and frequency for each communication type.
Document the distribution channels for each segment.

steps.description: Define the cadence and calendar for internal communications.

outputs.name: communication-calendar
outputs.desc: Calendar showing what goes to whom and when

outputs.name: cadence-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for frequency (no segment receives more than N emails per week)

process: Set the send frequency for each communication type (weekly all-hands, monthly department, quarterly leadership).
Set the maximum email frequency per segment per week to avoid overload.
Build the annual communication calendar with recurring and one-time sends.
Align the calendar with business cycles (quarterly reviews, annual planning, holidays).

steps.description: Create the email templates for internal communications.

outputs.name: internal-templates
outputs.desc: Email templates for each communication type

outputs.name: approval-workflow
outputs.desc: Approval process for each communication type (who drafts, who reviews, who approves)

process: Design the templates for each communication type (all-hands, department, leadership, policy, event).
Define the approval workflow for each (author, reviewer, approver, send authority).
Set up the drafting and review timeline per template.
Document the template usage guidelines.

steps.description: Track readership and engagement for internal communications.

outputs.name: engagement-metrics
outputs.desc: Open rates, click rates, and read-through rates by communication type and segment

outputs.name: internal-communications-plan
outputs.desc: Complete internal communications plan covering audiences, cadence, templates, approvals, and metrics

process: Track open rates and click rates for each send.
Segment the engagement data by audience and communication type.
Identify the most and least engaging communication types.
Recommend adjustments based on engagement data.
Compile the full internal communications plan.
